무엇: Extraordinary reports filed by Tokyo-listed companies — Japan’s equivalent of a US Form 8-K.

major-shareholder-change.뜻: A change in who holds a major stake in the company

control-change.뜻: A change in the parent company, or in a subsidiary the rules treat as significant

ceo-change.뜻: A change in the representative director — the office a Japanese company files as its chief executive

material-event.뜻: An event the company states will materially affect its financial position, results or cash flows

material-event-group.뜻: The same, stated at group level rather than for the filer alone

subsidiary-acquisition.뜻: A decision to acquire another company as a subsidiary

share-exchange.뜻: A decision to exchange shares — the structure Japan uses to make one company a wholly owned subsidiary of another

merger.뜻: A decision to merge, with one company absorbing the other

company-split.뜻: A decision to split off part of a consolidated subsidiary into another company

reverse-split.뜻: A meeting called to decide on consolidating shares

agm-outcome.뜻: How the resolutions put to a shareholders meeting were voted

stock-options.뜻: Share options issued without a securities registration statement

financial-covenant.뜻: A covenant attached to the company’s borrowing — what would count as a breach

bad-debt.뜻: The company states a receivable may not be collected on time or at all

auditor-change.뜻: A change of the accounting firm that audits the company

governance-agreement.뜻: An agreement between the company and a shareholder about how it is run

offering-abroad.뜻: Shares or bonds offered or distributed outside Japan
